what: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees
title: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees
text: PASTRI infers directed cell-state transition matrix reconstructed lineage tree terminal-cell annotations. designed lineage trees derived CRISPR/Cas9 barcodes, somatic mutations, similar heritable marks. method infer transitions expression pseudotime. Instead, uses topology lineage tree: terminal cells whose latest common ancestor (LCA) close leaves treated observations short evolutionary separation, pairs sharing older LCA represent longer separation. PASTRI combines pairwise relationships across depth values, applies user-defined upper bounds encode allowed forbidden directions.

title: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees

title: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees
text: PASTRI runs four stages.

what: 1. Convert the lineage tree into pairwise LCA features
title: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees
text: calculate_lca_depths() reads Newick tree , every internal node, counts: distance_to_root: number edges node root; distance_to_farthest_leaf: maximum number descendant edges leaf. Let D_max largest distance_to_farthest_leaf tree. internal node, implementation calculates: Every unordered pair terminal nodes assigned metrics LCA. result contains node1, node2, subtree_root, lca_depth, lca_depth_norm, lca_normalized_height.
code: normalized_depth =   0.5 * (distance_to_root / D_max          + 1          - distance_to_farthest_leaf / D_max) lca_normalized_height = 1 - normalized_depth

what: 2. Estimate two-cell correlations at each depth
title: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees
text: Terminal nodes matched cell_info$nodeLabel assigned cell types. selected depth value d, PASTRI counts unordered cell-type pairs constructs symmetric two-cell correlation matrix (d). Cell-type frequencies among selected terminal cells used standardize matrix. depth values satisfying d <= fi_depth retained. Therefore, fi_depth depth cutoff, optimization tolerance.

what: 3. Recover one transition matrix per depth
title: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees
text: retained (d), PASTRI: standardizes correlation matrix cell-type frequencies; performs eigendecomposition; truncates negative eigenvalues zero; rescales eigenvalues depth-dependent power 1 / (2 * d); removes negative undefined entries; normalizes every column sum one. returned matrices, columns start cell types rows end cell types. Thus matrix["C5", "C4"] inferred transition strength C4 C5.

what: 4. Apply constraints and obtain the consensus matrix
title: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees
text: mean depth-specific matrices initializes L-BFGS-B optimization. PASTRI minimizes sum Frobenius distances candidate matrix T depth-specific matrices: , ||.||_F denotes Frobenius norm. Bound_Matrix supplies element-wise upper bounds: 0 forbids transition; Inf leaves transition unconstrained ; finite positive value sets numerical upper bound. bound matrix must dimensions cell-type order cell_type_list. optimization, negative/undefined entries removed columns normalized .
code: minimize over T:  sum over d of ||T - T(d)||_F

title: Inferring Cell State Transition Probabilities on Lineage Trees
code: library(PASTRI)  # 1. Load the example lineage tree. tree_file <- system.file("extdata", "HSC.nwk", package = "PASTRI")  # 2. Calculate pairwise LCA features. node_pair_depth <- calculate_lca_depths(   tree.path = tree_file,   mc.cores = 1 )  # 3. Load terminal-cell annotations. cell_file <- system.file("extdata", "HSC_nodeInfos.csv", package = "PASTRI") cell_info <- read.csv(cell_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)  # The order defines the row/column order of every matrix. cell_types <- c("C4", "C5", "C6", "C7", "C8")  # 4. Encode an irreversible progression C4 -> C5 -> C6 -> C7 -> C8. # Rows are destinations and columns are sources. Entries above the diagonal # represent backward transitions and are forbidden here. bound_matrix <- matrix(   Inf,   nrow = length(cell_types),   ncol = length(cell_types),   dimnames = list(cell_types, cell_types) ) bound_matrix[upper.tri(bound_matrix)] <- 0  # 5. Infer the constrained transition matrix. result <- get_optimal_transition_matrix(   node_pair_depth = node_pair_depth,   cell_info = cell_info,   Sel_u = "lca_normalized_height",   fi_depth = 0.2,   Bound_Matrix = bound_matrix,   cell_type_list = cell_types,   mc.cores = 1 )  # Column = start state; row = end state. result$optimal_matrix  # Long-form representation of the same matrix. head(result$optimal_norm_df_dataframe)

what: Calculate Transition Matrix from Two-Cell Correlation — calculate_transition_matrix
title: Calculate Transition Matrix from Two-Cell Correlation — calculate_transition_matrix
text: function calculates cell transition matrices based two-cell correlation matrices (d). first computes frequency cell type (using single-leaf nodes), builds standardized cell type combination avoid duplicate counts. Using node pair depth data selected depth measure (e.g., "lca_normalized_height" "lca_depth"), function computes correlation frequencies depth value d. depth d (maximum threshold fi_depth), corresponding transition matrix computed using eigenvalue decomposition, eigenvalues adjusted according depth. Finally, average transition matrix depths used initial guess optimization procedure (via L-BFGS-B method) derive optimal transition matrix.

title: Get Optimal Transition Matrix — get_optimal_transition_matrix
text: Compute optimal cell transition matrix integrating node-pair depth information per-cell annotations. function: (1) filters terminal (single-leaf) cells selected cell types, (2) calls calculate_transition_matrix() infer best transition matrix structural constraints, (3) flattens matrix long data frame start/end cell-type pairs normalized transition strengths, (4) labels results evaluated depth cutoff. version Windows-safe: internal parallelism automatically coerced single-core Windows vignette building (pkgdown) fail 'mc.cores' > 1 supported Windows.

title: Get Optimal Transition Matrix — get_optimal_transition_matrix
text: node_pair_depth data frame containing node pair depth information (e.g. calculate_lca_depths()). cell_info data frame per-cell info; must contain least cellNum celltype. rows cellNum == 1 retained (terminal leaves), filtered provided cell_type_list. Sel_u Character string choosing depth/height measure use node_pair_depth (e.g. "lca_normalized_height"). fi_depth Numeric. Depth cutoff / threshold passed calculate_transition_matrix(). Bound_Matrix Numeric matrix encoding constraints (e.g. irreversible transitions). Diagonal/upper-triangular structure often encodes prior directionality. cell_type_list Character vector cell types interest, order defines transition structure. mc.cores Integer. Desired parallel cores. Windows silently coerced 1. non-Windows coerced least 1.
